subject.title: Slug alias quota (25) blocking legitimate naming migration — publisher nitishgargiitd

question: Should this verified publisher receive a one-time, audited exception for the 13 enumerated historical slug aliases, or should it first release selected existing redirects under a defined retention policy?
rationale: Current main intentionally enforces the cap, but selecting an account-specific exception versus a redirect-retention policy changes the anti-squatting and ownership contract; source inspection cannot safely choose that policy.

options.title: Approve a scoped exception
options.body: Authorize exactly the 13 listed aliases for the verified publisher, retain the global quota for everyone else, and audit the override.

options.title: Release selected redirects first
options.body: Keep the hard quota and ask the publisher to propose low-value historical aliases for an authorized release based on a documented retention criterion.

options.title: Change the general policy
options.body: Increase or redesign the global quota only after defining broad anti-squatting, redirect-retention, and migration guarantees.

recommendation.title: Approve a scoped exception
recommendation.body: Authorize exactly the 13 listed aliases for the verified publisher, retain the global quota for everyone else, and audit the override.

likelyOwner.reason: Their merged work is the closest available history connection to the slug-protection policy that an exception would affect.
